names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 1 mai, «Sfânta Cuvioasă Isidora».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Μαΐου, «Οσία Ισιδώρα η δια Χριστόν Σαλή», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 10 May, „Преподобна Исидора Јуродива.“ — Преподобна left off, which is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types`, and Јуродива left off too, which is the `fool-for-christ` it also carries and which BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5's table reads as a rank and not an epithet. Nothing else is in the heading: Tabennisi, the feigned madness, Pitirim and the year are all in the body. A direct walk of every `names` entry in `saints/` finds no folder holding Исидора — not `isidora-17-october`, which has no Serbian form — so this one folds with nothing, and it does not meet the ten `isidore-*` folders either, whose names are masculine.

The heading of the calendar’s name link, «Исидора Тавенская, Христа ради юродивая, прп.», with the rank and the epithet of folly left off, which leaves the forename and the monastery. The day’s own line declines her «Прп Исидоры, Христа ради юродивой (VI)». `fk.mjs` returned NONE before the write.

floruit.note: doxologia.ro, Viața Sfintei Cuvioase Isidora: «Această cuvioasă maică s-a nevoit în Mănăstirea Tabena sau Tabenisioților din Egipt în veacul al IV-lea».

death.note: saint.gr: «Η Οσία Ισιδώρα, αφού ασκήτεψε θεοφιλώς σε μονή της Αιγύπτου, κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 365 μ.Χ.» The Romanian life on doxologia.ro gives no year and does not agree about her end, having her leave the monastery after her sanctity was disclosed with nobody knowing where she went or how she died.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 10 мая ст. ст. — «Прп Исидоры , Христа ради юродивой (VI).»

attestations.note: The identification is exact: the calendar’s life names her «Исидора Тавенская, Христа ради юродивая», the fool for Christ of the Tabennisi monastery in Egypt, with the rag on her head, the kitchen work and the visit of the hermit Питирим sent by an angel — the same woman the Serbian row of this folder already keeps on the julian 10 May. **The Romanian and Greek rows of this folder stand on 1 May and were not moved**: that is a menologion number nine days off, not the thirteen-day style conversion, so BRIEF.md §8’s rule does not reach it, and one row per church is the schema. *An author may want to know that the calendars number this day differently.* `dates` was NOT touched, and the reason is that the Russian life contradicts itself about her century in the space of two paragraphs: it opens «подвизалась в Тавенском монастыре (Египет) в VI веке», the sixth century, and closes «Предполагают, что она скончалась не позднее 365 года», it is supposed she died not later than 365 — a date two centuries earlier, and given as a supposition. The folder’s floruit of the fourth century, read off doxologia, agrees with the second of those and not the first. Both readings are in the new paragraph and neither was made a field. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 1 mai — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Isidora»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Μαΐου — «Οσία Ισιδώρα η δια Χριστόν Σαλή»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps her — which the folder's Romanian note already said the Greek Church was expected to do, and this is the verification of it. It is plainly the same woman: the fool for Christ's sake in an Egyptian convent whose sanctity was revealed to the elder Pityrion. **The Greek adds a year of death the folder did not have**, «κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 365 μ.Χ.», which is inside the folder's fourth-century floruit and is now in `dates`; but the two sources do not agree on her end — the Romanian life has her leave the monastery after the visit with nobody knowing where she went or how she died, and saint.gr has her fall asleep in peace in a monastery of Egypt, so the year is recorded as traditional with the disagreement said in its note. The Greek names the visitor Pityrion and gives his day, 29 Νοεμβρίου; the corpus holds no folder for him, so no `related` row is added. **It prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both proper and naming her**, and they are stored here; two megalynaria and an oikos are also printed and were left, being kinds this corpus does not hold.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.05.2026 (10. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобна Исидора Јуродива.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry. **THE SERBIAN ROW IS THE JULIAN 10 MAY WHERE THE ROMANIAN AND THE GREEK ROWS ARE 1 MAY, AND THAT IS NOT A MISTAKE: A SECOND SLAVIC BOOK NOW CORROBORATES THE SLAVIC DAY.** This folder's `russian` row carries the note that „The Romanian life adds that the Russian Church keeps her on 10 May, which is not verified here“ — and the Ohrid Prologue, a Slavonic book reckoning in the Julian calendar, prints her on exactly that 10 May. One attestation row per church is the schema, so each church keeps the day it was read on and nothing moved; her `russian` row stays `undocumented`, because days.pravoslavie.ru has still not been opened for her and a claim is not made from a second-hand sentence. **It is plainly the same woman**: „била монахиња у женском манастиру у Тавенисиоту“, the convent of Tabennisi this folder is named for, feigning madness to hide her virtue and her struggle. **THE ENTRY RESOLVES, FROM ONE PAGE, WHAT THE FOLDER HELD AS A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO.** Its `death` note says doxologia has her leave the monastery with nobody knowing where she went or how she died, while saint.gr has her fall asleep in peace in a monastery of Egypt in 365 — and the Prologue gives **both halves together**: „А она да би избегла почаст од људи, одбеже из манастира, и умре незнано где, око 365. године.“ She fled the monastery to escape honour from men, and died nobody knows where, about 365. **The year agrees exactly and nothing in `dates` was touched**, and the fourth century „Живела у IV веку“ agrees with the `floruit` too; what changed is that the two readings are no longer only two books apart. **New here**: that she did the filthiest work, fed on the slops from the dishes, served everyone and was despised by everyone; that an angel of God disclosed the secret about her to the great ascetic Питирим; that he came to the convent, and seeing her bowed to the ground before her, and she to him; that when the sisters told him she was mad he answered „Ви сте луде ... а ова је већа пред Господом и од мене и од вас; ја само молим Бога, да мени да оно што је њој намењено на Суду Страшном!“; and that the sisters were ashamed and begged forgiveness of them both, and all began from then to show her honour — which is what she fled. **Питирим takes nothing and has no folder.** saint.gr names the same visitor Pityrion and gives him 29 Νοεμβρίου, and this folder's Greek note already says the corpus holds no folder for him; `pitirim-of-perm` is a Russian bishop and not him. No folder anywhere, so by the coordinator's third ruling no row is owed and no folder is minted, and he is named instead. **`types` untouched**: Преподобна is the `venerable` and Јуродива the `fool-for-christ` the folder already carries, and `monastic` is corroborated by „монахиња“. **No `locations`**: Tabennisi is named by three books now and this folder has never claimed a point for it. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Τὴν ὡραιότητα Χριστοῦ ποθήσασα, Μῆτερ τρισόλβιε, ὁδὸν τὴν σύντομον, τὴν ὁδηγούσαν πρὸς Αὐτόν, προείλου τὴν ταπείνωσιν, ὅθεν σε ἀνέδειξε, μοναζόντων διδάσκαλον, ἄκρον τε ὑπόδειγμα, τῆς Αὐτοῦ ἐκμιμήσεως, διὸ χαρμονικῶς σοι βοῶμεν, χαῖρε, ὢ Ἰσιδώρα παμμακάριστε.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ', Τὴν ὡραιότητα, on the page of «Οσία Ισιδώρα η δια Χριστόν Σαλή»

english.text: Having longed for the beauty of Christ, O thrice-blessed mother, thou didst choose humility, the short road that leads to Him; wherefore He showed thee forth a teacher of monastics and a highest example of the imitation of Himself. Therefore with joy we cry to thee: Rejoice, O all-blessed Isidora.

hymns.text: Ποθούσα τυχεῖν, τῆς ἄνω Μῆτερ στάσεως, ταχεῖαν ὁδόν, προείλου τὴν ταπείνωσιν, δι’ ἧς ἤχθης Χριστῷ ὡς καρπὸς εὐκλεὴς καὶ τερπνὸς Ἰσιδώρα παναοίδιμε, βραβεία λαμβάνουσα τὰ ἄφθαρτα.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β', Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν, on the page of «Οσία Ισιδώρα η δια Χριστόν Σαλή»

english.text: Longing to attain the state above, O mother, thou didst choose humility for the swift road, and by it wast brought to Christ as a fruit glorious and delightful, O all-renowned Isidora, receiving the incorruptible prizes.
